cards.front: What happens in the early and late phases of an allergic asthma attack?
cards.back: Allergic asthma is **type I hypersensitivity**. **Early phase** (minutes): allergen cross-links IgE on **mast cells**; histamine and leukotrienes cause bronchospasm. **Late phase** (hours): recruited **eosinophils** and Th2 cytokines cause inflammation, mucus and airway damage.
cards.back_pt: A asma alérgica é **hipersensibilidade tipo I**. **Fase precoce** (minutos): o alérgeno faz ligação cruzada da IgE nos **mastócitos**; histamina e leucotrienos causam broncoespasmo. **Fase tardia** (horas): **eosinófilos** recrutados e citocinas Th2 causam inflamação, muco e lesão da via aérea.

cards.front: Which two sputum findings are classic for asthma?
cards.back: **Curschmann spirals**: coiled plugs of mucus and shed epithelial cells that form in small airways. **Charcot-Leyden crystals**: thin, needle-shaped crystals made from a protein of **eosinophils**.
cards.back_pt: **Espirais de Curschmann**: tampões espiralados de muco e células epiteliais descamadas que se formam nas pequenas vias aéreas. **Cristais de Charcot-Leyden**: cristais finos, em forma de agulha, formados a partir de uma proteína dos **eosinófilos**.

cards.front: Which emphysema pattern does smoking cause, and which does alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency cause?
cards.back: **Smoking**: **centriacinar** emphysema; damage centers on the respiratory bronchioles and is worst in the **upper lobes**. **Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency**: **panacinar** emphysema; the whole acinus is damaged, worst in the **lower lobes**.
cards.back_pt: **Tabagismo**: enfisema **centroacinar**; a lesão se concentra nos bronquíolos respiratórios e é pior nos **lobos superiores**. **Deficiência de alfa-1 antitripsina**: enfisema **panacinar**; todo o ácino é lesado, pior nos **lobos inferiores**.

cards.front: What mechanism destroys alveolar walls in emphysema, and how does it change lung compliance?
cards.back: A **protease-antiprotease imbalance**. Smoke recruits neutrophils and macrophages that release **elastase**, and oxidants inactivate **alpha-1 antitrypsin**. Loss of elastic fibers **increases compliance** and lowers elastic recoil, so small airways collapse in expiration and trap air.
cards.back_pt: Um **desequilíbrio protease-antiprotease**. A fumaça recruta neutrófilos e macrófagos que liberam **elastase**, e os oxidantes inativam a **alfa-1 antitripsina**. A perda de fibras elásticas **aumenta a complacência** e reduz o recolhimento elástico, e as pequenas vias aéreas colapsam na expiração e retêm ar.

cards.front: What does the Reid index measure, and how does it change in chronic bronchitis?
cards.back: It is the thickness of the **mucous gland layer** divided by the thickness of the bronchial wall between the epithelium and the cartilage. **Mucous gland hyperplasia** in chronic bronchitis raises it **above 0.4** (normally below 0.4).
cards.back_pt: É a espessura da **camada de glândulas mucosas** dividida pela espessura da parede brônquica entre o epitélio e a cartilagem. A **hiperplasia das glândulas mucosas** na bronquite crônica eleva o índice **acima de 0,4** (normalmente abaixo de 0,4).

cards.front: Why can alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency damage the liver?
cards.back: In the **PiZZ** genotype, the misfolded protein is trapped in the **endoplasmic reticulum** of hepatocytes. It forms **PAS-positive, diastase-resistant globules** and can cause hepatitis and **cirrhosis**. The lung disease comes from the low serum level instead.
cards.back_pt: No genótipo **PiZZ**, a proteína mal dobrada fica retida no **retículo endoplasmático** dos hepatócitos. Ela forma **glóbulos PAS-positivos e resistentes à diástase** e pode causar hepatite e **cirrose**. Já a doença pulmonar vem do nível sérico baixo.

cards.front: In cystic fibrosis, why is sweat chloride high while airway mucus is thick?
cards.back: CFTR is an ATP-gated **chloride channel**. In **sweat ducts** it reabsorbs chloride, so its loss raises **sweat chloride**. In **airways** it secretes chloride; without it, **sodium absorption** rises, water follows the salt out of the airway lumen, and mucus becomes thick.
cards.back_pt: O CFTR é um **canal de cloreto** regulado por ATP. Nos **ductos sudoríparos** ele reabsorve cloreto, então sua perda eleva o **cloreto no suor**. Nas **vias aéreas** ele secreta cloreto; sem ele, a **absorção de sódio** aumenta, a água acompanha o sal para fora da luz da via aérea e o muco fica espesso.

cards.front: What is bronchiectasis, and what are its classic causes?
cards.back: Permanent **dilation of bronchi** after chronic infection and inflammation destroy the wall. Classic causes: **cystic fibrosis**, **Kartagener syndrome** (primary ciliary dyskinesia), **ABPA** (allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis), **tuberculosis** and airway obstruction (tumor or foreign body).
cards.back_pt: **Dilatação permanente dos brônquios** após infecção e inflamação crônicas destruírem a parede. Causas clássicas: **fibrose cística**, **síndrome de Kartagener** (discinesia ciliar primária), **ABPA** (aspergilose broncopulmonar alérgica), **tuberculose** e obstrução da via aérea (tumor ou corpo estranho).

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man has 1 year of slowly worsening shortness of breath on exertion. He has never smoked. His father died at age 52 of both liver disease and emphysema. Exam shows decreased breath sounds and a prolonged expiratory phase. Serum ALT is mildly elevated. Spirometry shows an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.58 that does not improve after a bronchodilator. Which pattern is chest CT most likely to show?
choices: Centriacinar emphysema most severe in the upper lobes
Paraseptal emphysema next to the pleura at the apices
Panacinar emphysema most severe in the lower lobes
Dilated, thick-walled bronchi with mucus plugs in the upper lobes
Reticular opacities with honeycombing at the lung bases
questions.explanation: Early emphysema in a nonsmoker with liver disease and a family history suggests **alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency**. Without enough antiprotease, elastase destroys the whole acinus, so the emphysema is **panacinar** and worst in the **lower lobes**. **Centriacinar**, upper-lobe emphysema is the pattern caused by **smoking**, which this man does not have. Basal honeycombing suggests pulmonary fibrosis, a restrictive disease with a normal or high FEV1/FVC ratio.
questions.explanation_pt: Enfisema precoce em um não fumante com doença hepática e história familiar sugere **deficiência de alfa-1 antitripsina**. Sem antiprotease suficiente, a elastase destrói todo o ácino, então o enfisema é **panacinar** e pior nos **lobos inferiores**. O enfisema **centroacinar** dos lobos superiores é o padrão causado pelo **tabagismo**, que este homem não tem. O faveolamento basal sugere fibrose pulmonar, uma doença restritiva com relação VEF1/CVF normal ou alta.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman has repeated episodes of wheezing, chest tightness and cough at night. The episodes start after contact with cats and during the spring. Between episodes, she feels well. During an episode, she has diffuse expiratory wheezes. A sputum sample shows coiled mucus casts and many thin, needle-shaped crystals. Her blood eosinophil count is high. The crystals are formed from a protein of which cell type?
choices: Eosinophils
Neutrophils
Mast cells
Alveolar macrophages
Th2 lymphocytes
questions.explanation: This is **allergic asthma**. The needle-shaped crystals are **Charcot-Leyden crystals**, formed from a protein of **eosinophils**, which arrive in the **late phase**. The coiled casts are **Curschmann spirals**. **Mast cells** drive the early phase through histamine and leukotrienes, but they do not form these crystals. Th2 cells recruit eosinophils through cytokines such as IL-5, but they are not the source of the crystals.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **asma alérgica**. Os cristais em forma de agulha são **cristais de Charcot-Leyden**, formados a partir de uma proteína dos **eosinófilos**, que chegam na **fase tardia**. Os moldes espiralados são **espirais de Curschmann**. Os **mastócitos** comandam a fase precoce por meio de histamina e leucotrienos, mas não formam esses cristais. As células Th2 recrutam eosinófilos por citocinas como a IL-5, mas não são a origem dos cristais.

questions.stem: A 4-year-old boy has had repeated pneumonias since infancy. Respiratory cultures grow Pseudomonas aeruginosa. He has frequent bulky, greasy, foul-smelling stools, and his weight is below the 5th percentile. As a newborn, he needed surgery for a bowel obstruction caused by thick meconium. His sweat chloride level is markedly elevated. Genetic testing shows that he is homozygous for the most common mutation that causes his disease. What is the effect of this mutation on the encoded protein?
choices: The protein reaches the cell membrane, but its channel does not open
A premature stop codon prevents any protein from being made
A trinucleotide repeat expansion silences the gene
The protein misfolds and is degraded before it reaches the cell membrane
The protein reaches the cell membrane and opens, but its pore conducts too little chloride
questions.explanation: Recurrent *Pseudomonas* infections, **pancreatic insufficiency**, **meconium ileus** and a high **sweat chloride** mean **cystic fibrosis**. The most common mutation is **ΔF508** in the **CFTR** gene on **chromosome 7**: the protein **misfolds**, is held in the endoplasmic reticulum and is degraded, so little reaches the membrane. A channel that reaches the membrane but does not open describes a different, less common class of CFTR mutation. A channel with a narrow pore that conducts too little chloride is another, milder class of CFTR mutation.
questions.explanation_pt: Infecções recorrentes por *Pseudomonas*, **insuficiência pancreática**, **íleo meconial** e **cloreto no suor** elevado indicam **fibrose cística**. A mutação mais comum é a **ΔF508** no gene **CFTR** no **cromossomo 7**: a proteína **se dobra de forma errada**, fica retida no retículo endoplasmático e é degradada, então pouca proteína chega à membrana. Um canal que chega à membrana mas não abre descreve outra classe de mutação do CFTR, menos comum. Um canal com poro estreito, que conduz pouco cloreto, é outra classe de mutação do CFTR, mais leve.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man with a 50-pack-year smoking history has 2 years of worsening shortness of breath. He has little cough or sputum. He is thin, breathes out through pursed lips and has a barrel-shaped chest. Breath sounds are decreased, and the chest is hyperresonant to percussion. Oxygen saturation is 93% on room air. Which set of pulmonary function results is most likely?
choices: FEV1/FVC decreased; TLC increased; DLCO normal
FEV1/FVC decreased; TLC increased; DLCO decreased
FEV1/FVC increased; TLC decreased; DLCO decreased
FEV1/FVC normal or increased; TLC decreased; DLCO normal
FEV1/FVC normal; TLC normal; DLCO decreased
questions.explanation: This is **emphysema** (the classic *pink puffer*). Obstruction lowers the **FEV1/FVC ratio**, and air trapping with **increased compliance** raises **TLC**. Destruction of alveolar walls removes surface area and capillaries, so **DLCO falls**. An obstructive pattern with a **normal DLCO** fits asthma or chronic bronchitis, where the alveolar walls are intact.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **enfisema** (o clássico *pink puffer*, "soprador rosado"). A obstrução reduz a **relação VEF1/CVF**, e o aprisionamento de ar com **aumento da complacência** eleva a **CPT**. A destruição das paredes alveolares remove superfície e capilares, então a **DLCO cai**. Um padrão obstrutivo com **DLCO normal** combina com asma ou bronquite crônica, em que as paredes alveolares estão preservadas.

notes.title: Obstructive lung disease: asthma, COPD, bronchiectasis and cystic fibrosis
notes.body_md:
## Obstructive pattern

- Airflow out of the lungs is limited, so **FEV1 falls more than FVC** and the **FEV1/FVC ratio is low**.
- Air trapping raises **RV** and often **TLC**.

## Asthma

- Reversible bronchospasm from **type I hypersensitivity** (Th2 cells, IgE, mast cells, **eosinophils**).
- Triggers: allergens, viral infections, cold air, exercise and smoke.
- Sputum: **Curschmann spirals** and **Charcot-Leyden crystals**.
- **Aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease**: asthma, **nasal polyps** and attacks after aspirin or other NSAIDs. COX blockade shifts arachidonic acid toward **leukotrienes**.
- **Methacholine challenge**: hyperresponsive airways narrow easily; useful when baseline spirometry is normal.

## COPD

- Mostly caused by **smoking**; emphysema and chronic bronchitis often occur together.
- **Emphysema**: a **protease-antiprotease imbalance** destroys alveolar walls. **Compliance increases**, elastic recoil falls and **DLCO is low**. Classic *pink puffer*: thin, pursed-lip breathing, **barrel chest**.
- **Chronic bronchitis**: a **clinical diagnosis**, a productive cough for at least 3 months in each of 2 consecutive years. **Mucous gland hyperplasia** raises the **Reid index**. Classic *blue bloater*: cyanosis, CO2 retention and edema from cor pulmonale.

## Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency

- **PiZZ** genotype; low serum levels leave the lungs unprotected: early **panacinar** emphysema in the **lower lobes**, worse with smoking.
- Liver: misfolded protein stays in hepatocytes as **PAS-positive globules**; it can cause **cirrhosis**.

## Bronchiectasis

- Permanent **dilation of bronchi** after chronic infection and inflammation.
- Causes: **cystic fibrosis**, **Kartagener syndrome**, **ABPA**, **tuberculosis** and airway obstruction.
- Large volumes of purulent sputum, recurrent infections, **hemoptysis** and clubbing.

## Cystic fibrosis

- Autosomal recessive; **CFTR** gene on **chromosome 7**; most common mutation **ΔF508** (misfolded protein that is degraded).
- Less chloride secretion and more sodium absorption make secretions thick. **Sweat chloride is high**.
- **Meconium ileus**, **pancreatic insufficiency** (steatorrhea, low fat-soluble vitamins), lung infections (***Pseudomonas***, *S. aureus*) and **male infertility** (absent vas deferens).
notes.body_pt_md:
## Padrão obstrutivo

- O fluxo expiratório é limitado, então o **VEF1 cai mais que a CVF** e a **relação VEF1/CVF fica baixa**.
- O aprisionamento de ar eleva o **VR** e muitas vezes a **CPT**.

## Asma

- Broncoespasmo reversível por **hipersensibilidade tipo I** (células Th2, IgE, mastócitos, **eosinófilos**).
- Gatilhos: alérgenos, infecções virais, ar frio, exercício e fumaça.
- Escarro: **espirais de Curschmann** e **cristais de Charcot-Leyden**.
- **Doença respiratória exacerbada por ácido acetilsalicílico**: asma, **pólipos nasais** e crises após ácido acetilsalicílico ou outros AINEs. O bloqueio da COX desvia o ácido araquidônico para os **leucotrienos**.
- **Teste de broncoprovocação com metacolina**: vias aéreas hiper-responsivas se estreitam facilmente; útil se a espirometria basal for normal.

## DPOC

- Causada sobretudo pelo **tabagismo**; enfisema e bronquite crônica costumam coexistir.
- **Enfisema**: um **desequilíbrio protease-antiprotease** destrói as paredes alveolares. A **complacência aumenta**, o recolhimento elástico cai e a **DLCO fica baixa**. Clássico *pink puffer* ("soprador rosado"): magro, respiração com lábios semicerrados, **tórax em tonel**.
- **Bronquite crônica**: **diagnóstico clínico**, tosse produtiva por pelo menos 3 meses em cada um de 2 anos consecutivos. A **hiperplasia das glândulas mucosas** eleva o **índice de Reid**. Clássico *blue bloater* ("inchado azul"): cianose, retenção de CO2 e edema por cor pulmonale.

## Deficiência de alfa-1 antitripsina

- Genótipo **PiZZ**; o nível sérico baixo deixa os pulmões sem proteção: enfisema **panacinar** precoce nos **lobos inferiores**, pior com tabagismo.
- Fígado: a proteína mal dobrada fica retida nos hepatócitos como **glóbulos PAS-positivos**; pode causar **cirrose**.

## Bronquiectasia

- **Dilatação permanente dos brônquios** após infecção e inflamação crônicas.
- Causas: **fibrose cística**, **síndrome de Kartagener**, **ABPA**, **tuberculose** e obstrução da via aérea.
- Muito escarro purulento, infecções recorrentes, **hemoptise** e baqueteamento digital.

## Fibrose cística

- Autossômica recessiva; gene **CFTR** no **cromossomo 7**; mutação mais comum **ΔF508** (proteína mal dobrada que é degradada).
- Menos secreção de cloreto e mais absorção de sódio tornam as secreções espessas. O **cloreto no suor é alto**.
- **Íleo meconial**, **insuficiência pancreática** (esteatorreia, deficiência de vitaminas lipossolúveis), infecções pulmonares (***Pseudomonas***, *S. aureus*) e **infertilidade masculina** (ausência dos ductos deferentes).
